propositions: Read-only Git probes in tests/_isolation.py (porcelain and head) invoke subprocess.run without timeout, allowing a blocked Git child to keep pytest alive indefinitely after test completion.

A deterministic blocking-git shim injected into PATH confirmed the post-test hook boundary—the real subprocess hung in _isolation.py with no timeout, distinguishing the missing inner watchdog from test-body hangs or pytest teardown.
Both probes must apply a fixed 5-second timeout watchdog and explicitly surface subprocess.TimeoutExpired as an isolation-infrastructure failure rather than collapsing it to None.

Test monkeypatches of the shared subprocess module contaminate the autouse teardown guard unless the real runner is bound at import, so _isolation.py must capture subprocess.run once and route both probes through that stable boundary.
